cards.text: New letter, friend! Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth again, and to all the saints throughout Achaia. And he didn't write this one solo, because there's a second name signed at the bottom, like a group card at work.

cards.question: Paul's letter to the church in Corinth has a second name on it. Who's writing with him?
True or false: Paul says he's an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God.

cards.text: Then the greeting, and Paul skips the small talk. No "hope this letter finds you well." Just grace and peace, and he says exactly who it's from.

cards.question: Paul sends the Corinthians grace and peace. Who does he say it comes from?

answers.text: God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
Paul and Timothy and the apostles
The saints in the church at Jerusalem

cards.text: Most of us open an email and go STRAIGHT to the problem. Paul opens his letter and breaks into praise: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.question: Paul calls God the Father of compassion and the God of all ___.

cards.text: And Paul says God comforts us in ALL our troubles. Not some. ALL. The big ones, the messy ones, the staring-at-the-ceiling-at-two-in-the-morning ones.

cards.question: God comforts Paul and his team in all their troubles. Why, according to Paul?

answers.text: So they can comfort others in trouble
So they never face trouble again
So they can rest from all their work

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the comfort his team gives to others is the comfort they received from God.

cards.text: Then Paul lines up two things that both overflow, like my bowl when I get a little too happy with the chocolate chips. First, he says the sufferings of Christ overflow to us.

cards.question: The sufferings of Christ overflow to Paul and his team. Through Christ, what else overflows?

cards.text: Paul's team has hard days and good days. Some days they're afflicted, some days they're comforted, and Paul says BOTH kinds of days are for somebody.

cards.question: Paul says his team's hard days and good days are both for the comfort of whom?
Paul says that comfort produces patient ___ in the Corinthians as they go through the same sufferings his team goes through.
Paul says his hope for the Corinthians is sure. Why?

answers.text: They share his sufferings and will share his comfort
They have never had to suffer for anything
They have already fixed every problem they had

cards.text: Then Paul gets honest about the hardships his team faced in the province of Asia. No thumbs-up emoji in the group chat pretending everything's fine. He tells it STRAIGHT.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians about his team's hardships in the province of Asia. How heavy was that burden?

answers.text: Far beyond their ability to endure
Heavy but easy enough to manage
Lighter than they had first feared

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the burden got so heavy that his team despaired even of life.

cards.text: Paul says they felt they were under the sentence of death. And here I was thinking a junk drawer was rough, so I'm just gonna quietly sit back down on my gold base.

cards.question: Paul's team felt they were under the sentence of death. Paul says it happened so they would not trust in whom?
Instead, Paul's team would trust in God. Facing a sentence of death, what does Paul say this God does?

cards.text: And God came through, friend. Paul says He delivered them from such a deadly peril.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says that now that God has delivered them once, they shouldn't count on Him to do it again.

cards.text: Paul's hope is set on God to deliver them yet again. And he doesn't leave the Corinthians sitting on the bench. He puts them in the game.

cards.question: Paul tells the Corinthians they help his team by their ___.

cards.text: And when God shows Paul's team favor in answer to those prayers, many will give thanks on their behalf. One rescue and a WHOLE crowd of thank-yous? Now THAT'S a batch I want coming out of my oven.
